    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersHarbour pork and prawn dumplingsSteamed pork, prawn and shiitake dumplings with chilli oilHow to make it300g pork mince150g green prawns, chopped1 tbsp grated ginger50g shiitake mushrooms, chopped1 tbsp soy sauce24 wonton wrappers2 tbsp chilli oilMix the pork, prawns, ginger, shiitake and soy.Spoon into the wonton wrappers and pinch up the sides.Steam until cooked through.Serve with chilli oil.Han's island tournament spring rollsCrisp rolls of cabbage, carrot, shiitake and glass noodles with sweet chilliHow to make it2 cups of shredded wombok1 carrot, grated100g shiitake mushrooms, sliced50g glass noodles1 tbsp soy sauce16 spring rolls of wrappers1 L vegetable oil, for frying100ml sweet chilli sauceSoak the glass noodles and prepare the vegetables.Stir-fry the wombok, carrot and shiitake.Add the noodles and soy.Cool the filling.Roll tight in the wrappers.Fry at 180°C until golden.Serve hot with the sweet chilli sauce for dipping.Sichuan salt and pepper squidHong Kong street foodHow to make itAs written, serves 4Scored squid dusted in rice flour and Sichuan salt and pepper, fried hard and fast, tossed with fried garlic, chilli and spring onion, with lemon.Cut 600g cleaned squid tubes open, score the inside in a crisscross and cut into strips.Toast 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, grind with 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp white pepper and mix with 100g rice flour.Toss the squid in the flour and fry in 190°C oil for 60 seconds until just crisp.Stir-fry 3 sliced garlic cloves, a sliced red chilli and 2 spring onions for 30 seconds, toss with the squid and serve with lemon.MainsMirror room char siu with fried riceHoney hoisin glazed roast pork neck with egg fried riceHow to make it800g pork neck4 tbsp hoisin sauce2 tbsp soy sauce2 tbsp honey1 tsp five spice2 tbsp Shaoxing wine300g cooked jasmine rice2 eggs3 spring onionsCook 120g jasmine rice ahead (the day before is best), spread it out and chill. Cold rice fries and holds better.Mix the hoisin, soy, honey, five spice and Shaoxing and coat the pork.Marinate overnight.Roast at 200°C, glazing twice.Rest the pork.Fry the rice with the eggs and spring onion.Slice the pork over the rice.Han's five-spice crispy duck pancakesThe lavish feast on Han's islandHow to make itAs written, serves 4Duck legs salted overnight, rubbed with five-spice and roasted until the skin crackles, shredded into steamed pancakes with cucumber, spring onion and hoisin.Rub 4 duck legs with 2 tsp salt and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight.Rub with 2 tsp five spice and roast skin up on a rack at 180°C for 90 minutes, then 10 minutes at 220°C until crisp.Shred the meat and skin with two forks.Steam 20 Chinese pancakes for 3 minutes.Serve with batons of a cucumber, shredded spring onion and a bowl of hoisin sauce.SweetsMango pancakesThin crepes wrapped around whipped cream and fresh mangoHow to make it120g plain flour2 eggs300ml full cream milk2 tbsp caster sugar300ml thickened cream2 mangoesWhisk the flour, eggs, milk and sugar and rest.Cook 8 thin crepes in a non-stick pan and cool.Whip the cream and slice the mango.Wrap each crepe around cream and a thick slice of mango.Fold into parcels and chill for an hour.DrinksIced chrysanthemum and goji honey teaChilled chrysanthemum tea with goji berries, rock sugar and honeyHow to make it1.2 L water15g dried chrysanthemum flowers2 tbsp goji berries50g rock sugar1 tbsp honey1 lemon1 bag iceBring the water to the boil and take off the heat.Add the chrysanthemum, goji and rock sugar and steep, stirring until the sugar melts.Strain, keeping the goji berries, and stir in the honey.Cool, then chill for an hour.Pour over ice in four glasses, drop in a few goji berries and add a squeeze of lemon.
